I1.quote: Hydrogen adsorption/desorption excess sorption measurements were performed with a volumetric Sieverts apparatus.
I1.location: main, p. 3, main text, left column, last paragraph

I2.quote: In this communication, we present 77 K isotherm data and sorption enthalpies for activated CA (ACAs) with BET surface areas up to 3200 m2/g as well as for metal-doped CAs.
I2.location: main, p. 3, main text, left column, second paragraph

I3.quote: We report the hydrogen surface excess sorption saturation value of 5.3 wt% at 30 bar pressure at 77 K, from an activated carbon aerogel with a surface area of 3200 m2/g
I3.location: main, p. 5, Abstract for web publication

I4.quote: The BET surface area of 3200 m²/g is the highest value that we are aware of for a CA.
I4.location: main, p. 3, main text, left column, second paragraph

I5.quote: A basic understanding of hydrogen sorption behavior of materials will be critical to the transportation sector needs of high gravimetric and volumetric density.
I5.location: main, p. 3, main text, first sentence

notes: The PDF is the LLNL report version (UCRL-JRNL-227848) of the Chemistry of Materials communication: a primary article with original data, not a thesis or review. Measured carbon sorbents are CO2-activated carbon aerogels (BET 1460-3200 m2/g) and Ni-/Co-doped carbon aerogels (BET 970 and 1100 m2/g quoted for the Ni samples); the 330 m2/g organic aerogel is uncarbonized and is not a carbon sorbent. Further 77 K values: Figure 1 isotherms (pressure axis 0-40 bar) and Table 1 saturation values. Supporting Information (Figure 1S, Ni/Co-CA isotherms) is cited but not among the input files. No retraction notice and no statement that the uptake values were published before.
